checks: Served study and canonical data match the workspace files used by this run.
All 34 newer floors show data-derived single/accessible/WG3/WG4 inventories and the original-outline estimate label.
Every WG card and representative single, accessible, common-space and circulation cards retain the correct semantics.
Newer apartment measurements describe bounding polygons, never clear living area; old furnishing controls are absent.
Visible direct door cards open; collision-hidden door icons are enumerated per floor rather than treated as missing openings.
All six houses have responsive ground-floor checks in both themes at 1440, 390 and 320 pixels without clipped cards or horizontal overflow.
House 55 and House 51 top-floor cards retain their old clear-room dimensions and optional furnishing concepts.
The 34 overview PNGs support visual review of room packing, unassigned gray areas and circulation.

observations: Single-floor geometry presents perimeter rooms, a connected hall and a distinct stair/lift core, with unused area left gray.
Blue upper floor shows three whole WG envelopes with independent hall entrances and no invented bedroom partitions.
The 320px day view keeps controls, labels and the floor within the viewport.
WG measurements and uncertainty text are readable without old furniture controls.
Grey 2. OG shows 13 single envelopes with the unmatched corner and loggia allowance left gray; the source perimeter stays intact.

limitations: This browser check verifies the displayed estimates and interaction; it does not confirm actual apartment or WG locations.

Ninety-nine door labels across the 34 desktop floors are hidden by collision handling. Their exact titles are listed per floor; the openings remain in the geometry and all ten WG space cards are accessible.
